cited_by.label: 2H.1 You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.

precepts.text: Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps.
precepts.point: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite: the word Moor, Morasthite, is in the Bible. Micah, teacher of the Moors.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah names the same prophet: “Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and spake to all the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.”

It confirms Micah 1:1: the word of the Lord came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and it was a word against Jerusalem. Morasthite: the Moor is in the Bible, and Micah was a teacher of the Moors.

And what Micah prophesied is what happened to us, over and over. Anytime we are set somewhere, we rise up as a nation, and the Lord allows Esau to conquer us. Why? Because the savior is Christ. If we could do it without Christ, why would we need Christ? The Moors went into Europe in 710 AD and brought universities, soap, the holy waters that became rubbing alcohol, strawberries, olives and grapes, wine, even chess; then they were conquered and scattered, many sent to Africa and transported to Brazil and North America. Zion plowed like a field, Jerusalem become heaps.

precepts.text: Speak all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.
precepts.why:
From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word. Jeremiah was told: “Stand in the court of the Lord’s house, and speak unto all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in the Lord’s house, all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word”.

All the words, not some of them. So do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity. Moses, Jeremiah, Christ and John all carry the same charge: neither add nor diminish.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
This is where the Most High said he would do something for Jeremiah: “Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.” That is why a man was with Jeremiah when the people sought his life.

That is a message to us. As long as we stay true to the Most High’s word, the Most High may have our enemies show mercy on us. It depends on who we are. Urijah: the Most High did not have mercy on him; it was meant for Urijah to be put to death. Jeremiah was not meant to be taken to Babylon like Daniel and Ezekiel; Jeremiah was meant to stay. The Most High has different situations happen for different people, different brothers, different prophets.

Nevertheless, for some of us he will have our enemies show mercy on us, as long as we stay true and faithful. He does promise this thing: the enemy will entreat you well.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
“Therefore now amend your ways and your doings, and obey the voice of the Lord your God; and the Lord will repent him of the evil that he hath pronounced against you.” If you amend your ways and obey, God will repent him of the evil.

Understand: every time you sin, God is pronouncing evil against you. We don’t understand what goes on in that other realm; there are conversations happening while you are in the midst of that wickedness: God is going to bring some evil into your life. And it’s a spectrum. We don’t want no smoke with God. Trust me.

moments.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: If so be they will hearken, and turn every man from his evil way, that I may repent me of the evil which I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings. God wants you to take heed and turn.

The Lord sends his prophets every morning, rising up early, and the people do not hearken; then when the fire comes they blame God. Look at the platform being built, brothers travelling to other countries, and ask whether you are doing enough instead of sitting on the couch pumped up on evil.

In the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign the Most High commands Jeremiah to stand in the court of the Lord's house and speak all His words to the cities of Judah, diminishing not a word, that they might hearken and turn from their evil way.
If they will not hearken and walk in His law, He will make this house like Shiloh and this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.
When Jeremiah finished speaking all that the Most High commanded, the priests, the prophets, and all the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die.

They were angry that he prophesied the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate; this is the same thing we go through when we read the Bible to people and tell them thus saith the Lord, and they get mad and want to harm us.

When the princes of Judah heard, they came up from the king's house and sat in the entry of the new gate, and the priests and prophets said this man is worthy to die for prophesying against this city.

It was not about Jeremiah speaking the word of the Most High but about their feelings getting hurt; he prophesied only because the Most High told him what to say, the same way people today say you cannot speak against this country when we are only saying what the Bible says.

Jeremiah answers the princes and all the people that the Most High sent him to prophesy against this house and city, and tells them to amend their ways and obey, that the Most High might repent of the evil pronounced against them.

He puts himself in their hand to do as they see good, but warns that if they put him to death they bring innocent blood upon themselves and upon the city, for of a truth the Most High sent him to speak these words.

The princes and all the people then say to the priests and prophets that this man is not worthy to die, for he has spoken in the name of the Most High; our people were rebellious but they were not that dumb.

The elders rise and recall that Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah that Zion would be plowed like a field, yet Hezekiah did not put him to death but feared the Most High, who then repented of the evil.

The elders also recall Urijah the son of Shemaiah, who prophesied against the city like Jeremiah; when Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but the king sent men who fetched him back and slew him with the sword.

One king knew the word came from the Most High and spared the prophet, while another king put his prophet to death; nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so he was not given to the people to be killed.

This is where it gets controversial; this is where it gets heated between Jeremiah and Israel because of what he is prophesying. Put yourself in the time of Jeremiah. Israel is being rebellious, but they are looking at Jeremiah like, you really don’t care about your own people. How can you say we are going to be destroyed? How can you say we are going to be killed by the king of Babylon, and you want us to submit to him and not fight back? So in their mind, we need to kill him. But Jeremiah says no: this message that I am telling you is what the Most High told me to tell you. Humble down and submit.
The Lord tells Jeremiah, “Stand in the court of the Lord’s house”, the temple, and speak to all that come to worship there “all the words that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a word”.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “If so be they will hearken, and turn every man from his evil way”. That has always been the message from the prophets: to listen, and to turn from the evil way, “that I may repent me of the evil, which I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings.”

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “If ye will not hearken to me, to walk in my law, which I have set before you, To hearken to the words of my servants the prophets”. See what the Most High is saying: if we will not listen and walk in his law, what is going to happen?

It is the same today. A lot of celebrities have been sharing our content. A Christian gospel singer responded to us and shared the video of what we did in Chicago, thousands of us marching. On the comment board you see some of our people: ‘they hate black women, they hate us, they hate their own people.’ And you see other people responding, ‘these brothers are for real, these brothers in purple and gold are serious.’ But you always get a lot of our people saying they hate us, they are against us, because we are telling our people God’s law and they are taking it as hatred. It is the same thing Jeremiah went through.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.” When Jeremiah had made an end of speaking, “the priests and the prophets and all the people took him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.” They grabbed Jeremiah: kill him, kill him, get rid of him. “Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh”?

That is the same reaction we get when we are teaching in Queens, in Brooklyn, in Kansas, in Chicago, in New Orleans. Our people look at us like, wait, what are y’all talking about, God is going to kill us, we are going to be destroyed? They grabbed Jeremiah and said, we are going to put this man to death.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “When the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king’s house”, and “Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die”. The priests and the prophets are against Jeremiah, while the princes of Judah and the people are considering what Jeremiah is saying. There is a division among the people: Jeremiah might be telling us the truth, versus the priests and the prophets saying no, he needs to be put to death.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Now Jeremiah speaks to the princes and to the people: “The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city”. He tells them the same thing he told them before: “amend your ways and your doings, and obey the voice of the Lord your God; and the Lord will repent him of the evil that he hath pronounced against you.”

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “As for me, behold, I am in your hand”: whatever you want to do to me, that is on you, but I am telling you what God told me. “But know ye for certain, that if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof”.

Christ told us this. When you examine the history, it was our people that killed the prophets. That is why we cannot seek love; we have to teach as it is written, because the Bible prophesied a remnant shall return. So you online, you listening, you have to decide within yourself: am I that remnant? Is it time for me to return? I have been watching online for four years and I have not fellowshipped. I need to make a decision. I need to get involved and do this work, and assist however I can.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “This man is not worthy to die: for he hath spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God.” The princes and the people listened to Jeremiah: he is saying the right thing. That happens to us in the street. Sometimes you get some of our people that say, this is true, what these brothers are saying is true, and you get a majority of our people saying these brothers have got to go. But look here: the Most High moved the spirits of the princes and the people to consider what Jeremiah was saying, and to say, he is right.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Certain of the elders of the land rose up and reminded the people of Micah the Morasthite, the Micah from the book of Micah, who prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah: “Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.” That is what Micah taught in those days.

The princes and the people are reminding the prophets and the priests. The prophets and the priests need to be reminded: what the hell is this? It goes to show you that during the time of Jeremiah there were a lot of false prophets, saying ‘peace, peace’ when God says there is no peace. It is the same thing today. Christian ministers and political leaders say we shall have peace, we can work with America, all we have to do is vote, just vote and a change will come one day. In other words, eventually there will be peace. But that is not what God says.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the Lord”? Hezekiah did not kill Micah, and the Lord repented of the evil. “Thus might we procure great evil against our souls”: if we kill Jeremiah, we bring great evil against our souls.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: There was also a man that prophesied in the name of the Lord, Urijah, “who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah”. King Jehoiakim heard what this prophet said, and “the king sought to put him to death: but when Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt”. Jehoiakim sent men into Egypt to go get the prophet so he could kill him, and they brought him to the king, “who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.”
See that? King Jehoiakim killed one of the prophets of the Most High. This is our people. This is our own race.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: But the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah: that brother was with Jeremiah, “that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.” The Most High said he would do something for Jeremiah.
